newsitem.title: USA: Sun Microsystems net surges on record sales.
newsitem.headline: Sun Microsystems net surges on record sales.

text.p: Computer workstation maker Sun Microsystems Inc. said its net income nearly doubled in its fiscal fourth quarter, boosted by record-level sales.

Profits climbed 94 percent to $237 million from $122 million in the year-ago period. Earnings per share surged to 61 cents vs. the year-ago figure of 31 cents, which included a one-time charge equal to 12 cents a share.
Revenues at the Mountain View, Calif.-based company climbed 26 percent to $2.5 billion from $2 billion in 1996's second quarter.
Sun's earnings, which were issued after the close of trading on Nasdaq, surpassed Wall Street's estimate of 59 cents a share, according to the First Call service.
Earlier Thursday, Sun Microsystems stock rose 56 cents a share to $45.56.

Sun Chief Financial Officer Michael Lehman said the company shipped a record number of systems in its fourth quarter. Lehman said the company added 800 people during the quarter and expected to accelerate hiring early in the new fiscal year in areas that will boost revenue growth.

"Our business model has never been stronger," Lehman told analysts in a conference call, adding that the company plans to price its products aggressively as part of its plan to continue transforming the company into one of the corporate world's top suppliers of computing systems.
